title: Thunderbird won't load
creator: aandw.gibbons
content: I had Thunderbird installed on my Windows 10 computer and on my Android tablet. I noticed that some emails were not going. After hours reading posts on the internet I changed from POP3 to IMAP. Now nothing works. I uninstalled Thunderbird from both my laptop and the tablet and then did a download and reinstall on each. In each case I could receive email but now could not send. In the end I am uninstalled from both devices and loaded another product called EMclient. It installed instantly and properly on both the laptop and the tablet. I would like to return to Thunderbird, in spite of the fact that I lost a lot of emails in folders from a number of years of using the product, but would certainly like a lot simpler installation than what I experienced. Mozilla needs to look at other products and determine why they install so easily and Thunderbird is so difficult. I can't provide the version of Thunderbird other than the version for the laptop was the latest from mozilla's website and the version for the tablet was downloaded from the Play store in both cases this evening.

title: Cannot send emails from Thunderbird - error MF-505
creator: jaycam
content:
For years I have had two email addresses: - @virginmedia.com and an older @blueyonder.co.uk one - with no problems: POP is set up with the two servers pop3.virginmedia.com and pop3.blueyonder.co.uk. SMTP is set up with smtp.virginmedia.com for both. Everything was sweetness and light. I could receive and send from both accounts no problems.

Two weeks ago, the MF-505 relay refused error popped up when I tried to send an email from @blueyonder.co.uk and has continued to do so ever since. I can receive @blueyonder.co.uk emails with no problems. I can receive and send from @virginmedia.com with no problems. I can login to the virginmedia webmail site with @blueyonder.co.uk and send emails with no problems. Even so, I changed the @blueyonder.co.uk mail app password with Virginmedia just in case; no help. I have deleted the saved passwords and resaved them; no help. I have tried adding an @blueyonder.co.uk smtp outgoing server to Thunderbird even though I never had to before; no help. I have checked smtp server outgoing settings - even though everything works fine for @virginmedia.com. No problems there.

The general advice "out there" seems to be wait and it will resolve itself but it's been two weeks and for what it's worth Virginmedia confirm there is no problems with my account or their services their end.

any suggestions will be appreciated.
